After an Industrial Revolution that started with sheep farming and ended with an empire that spanned the world, we entered a period of relentless decline that saw us begging the IMF for a bail-out loan as our economy hit rock bottom. The revolution that Thatcher ushered in was painful and cathartic.

She banned "secondary picketing", where affiliated industries would strike "in sympathy" with one another, paralysing the economy. If the coal miners were on strike, the trains would go on strike so that they could halt deliveries of coal. If the car plant was striking, the steel workers would also down tools, because the cars their comrades were making were made of steel.

In 1982 the British Falkland Islands were invaded by Argentina. Everyone told her to let it go. Britain was back on the map, with an abrupt halt to our sleepy decline.
